text:
maria: Heads up — I found a local dev crash bundle that got uploaded to the staging debug S3 bucket and it contains a .env dump with an API key. Not production, but still sensitive.

maria: snippet from the bundle (sanitized):
```
/var/tmp/dev-run-2026-03-17.log
ENV: DOCKER_COMPOSE_FILE=.env
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAEXAMPLE12345==
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=****************
panic: runtime error at worker.go:42
```

maria: The bundle path is s3://redwood-staging-debug/dev-bundles/2026-03-17-1234.tar.gz — the debug uploader auto-included /tmp. Who should approve immediate rotation and removal of the bundle?

jonah: Was that created from your laptop or a CI runner?

maria: Local laptop while reproducing a race. I used the debug uploader script which uploaded the whole /tmp folder. I stopped the upload but the object exists.

security-bot: Automated alert — secret-detection rule "env-inline" flagged object s3://redwood-staging-debug/dev-bundles/2026-03-17-1234.tar.gz at 2026-03-17T18:04:10Z. Marked severity: medium.

liam: Action list:
1) Remove the S3 object immediately: `aws s3 rm s3://redwood-staging-debug/dev-bundles/2026-03-17-1234.tar.gz`
2) Rotate the exposed access key (and any associated session tokens)
3) Revoke any long-lived sessions tied to that key
4) Scrub uploaded debug bundle from retention/backups

liam: Quick commands (run as infra-admin):
```bash
# deactivate access key
aws iam update-access-key --user-name staging-debug-user --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE12345 --status Inactive
# revoke sessions (example for federation tokens)
aws sts revoke-session --session-id <session-id>
# delete s3 object
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-staging-debug/dev-bundles/2026-03-17-1234.tar.gz
```

kevin: Approve rotation now. :white_check_mark: Also check if the key was KMS-wrapped somewhere (we've seen dev tooling wrap tokens). If wrapped by our KMS key alias/rdw-staging, consider re-wrapping secrets and rotating the customer-managed key if it's been widely used.

kevin: To check KMS usage: `aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/rdw-staging` and `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` to see recent grants. If the debug bundle contained any wrapped blobs, treat as high priority.

maria: Understood. I'll:
- run the `aws s3 rm` now (from infra-approved machine)
- open a rotation ticket INFR-4523 and assign to iam-oncall for key rotation
- scrub local instructions in the debug uploader to exclude /tmp and `.env` files

maria: Quick note for the runbook update, suggestion: change uploader to run this filter by default:
```bash
# exclude common env files and tmp dirs
zip -r debug.zip . -x "*.env" "*/tmp/*" "*/.cache/*"
```

jonah: Also add a scanner rule to detect docker-compose mounting `.env` into containers or printing env var dumps to stdout. We should catch this before upload.

kevin: Agreed. Add rule to secret-scanner: pattern match for `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and common env filenames in uploaded artifacts. Also consider adding a one-click cleanup job for debug-buckets.

maria: Done: I removed the object, opened INFR-4523, and scrubbed the local bundle. Leaving rotation to iam-oncall. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
